7. He also submits that after considering the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the recovery of huge amount of loan money, the Adalat passed an order of attachment before judgment assigning sound reasonings to satisfy the eventual decree to be passed against the defendants. Thereafter, the application filed by the defendant challenging the said order was rejected by assigning cogent reasons and therefore, the same does not liable to be interfered with by this Court. In support of his contentions, he submits the cases of Hosne Ara Begum vs Chairman, Court of Settlement, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 9, Nitu Poddar vs Eastern Bank Ltd., reported in 9 BLC 209, Mahmudul Haque (Md) vs Md Hedayetullah, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 128, Shamsunnahar Salam vs Md Wahidur Rahman, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 232, Prof Nurul Amin Bepari vs Vice-Chancellot; reported in 50 DLR 405. 

 9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and Annexures, thereto and legal position involves in the case thoroughly. 

 12. Order XXI, rules. 41 to 62 provide the procedure of attachment for execution of a decree. Order XXI, rules 58 to 62 specially provide the procedure as to how the objection filed against attachment be disposed of and attached property be released if it is illegally or wrongly attached. In view of the Order XXI, rule 58(1) of the CPC, the stranger may raise objection against the attachment order, if it is adversely affected him, as if he is a party to the suit. The application filed under 38 rule 8 be treated as Miscellaneous Case in view of the rule 774 of the Civil Rules and Orders (CRO), Vol-1. In the Miscellaneous Case, the claimant or objector has the opportunity to adduce evidence to show that at the date of the attachment he had some interest in, or was possessed of, the property attached, then the Adalat may release the property in view of Order XXI, rule 60 of the CPC. 

 16. In the case of Mahmudul Haque (Md) vs Md Hedayetullah, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 128 where it was held that where special statutory remedy is available then such remedy, as a matter of course, must be availed of first. In our view, remedy being available to the petitioner under the Code of Civil Procedure, any application under the writ jurisdiction is not maintainable. As the petitioner has remedy under Order XXXVIII, rule 8 of the CPC against the attachment order, therefore, the writ petition is hit by the doctrine of exhaustion. 

 17. Apart from the same, the case entails disputed question of facts. In the case of Shamsunnahar Salam vs Md Wahidur Rahman, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 232 it was held that a writ Court cannot and should not decide any disputed question of fact which requires evidence to be taken for settlement. 

 18. In the light of the above discussion, we are of the view that the writ petition is not maintainable. So it does not require to enter into the merit of the case. As the Rule has no substance, therefore, the same is liable to be discharged.
